messages:
emma: Heads up — after last night's KMS key rotation some users scoped to the 'viewer' role reported they could save project settings in Console. We have 2 support tickets and a customer repro clip. Anyone else seeing this or a related permission/inheritance regression?
juan: Noted. I saw a couple of alerts from the permissions-monitoring job. Did we roll the RBAC schema change (policy refactor) alongside the rotation? PR #2398 was scheduled yesterday.
ops-bot: Automated deploy: RBAC-service v2.4.1 -> prod at 2026-03-18T03:12:12Z by ci/cd.
li: I pulled the audit logs for the affected orgs. Looks like these entries: ```
2026-03-18T03:14:05Z audit_id=az-981 action=update_project_settings user=alice role=viewer outcome=success policy_version=1
2026-03-18T03:14:07Z audit_id=az-982 action=update_project_settings user=bob role=viewer outcome=success policy_version=2
```
li: Weird that we have mixed policy_version values in the same window — suggests inconsistent reads during rollout. Could be a race between policy cache invalidation and KMS-driven key change for role encryption.
aziz-devex: The support repro attached a short screen recording showing the Save button not gated, and the network trace shows a 200 from /api/projects/123/settings with X-User-Role: viewer.
juan: If policy_version=1 allowed and v2 denies, mixed reads could cause flip-flop. But here v2 seems to allow in one line. We need to confirm what change in #2398 altered: was there a change to default fallback behavior (implicit-write=false -> true)?
maya-sre: Triage proposal: 1) add a temporary server-side deny for project settings writes if role==viewer; 2) roll back RBAC-service to v2.4.0 if we confirm the refactor caused it; 3) collect full cache invalidation timeline and KMS rotation timeline. I can cut the hotpatch if ops agrees.
emma: +1 on temp deny. Customer impact looks limited to config edits but it's a real privilege escalation. Marking as sev3 for now.
juan: I'll dump the policy objects from the postgres store and the cache at the times around the rotation. Also checking KMS key version metadata — maybe the policy blobs were re-encrypted with the new key in-flight.
li: Repro steps I ran locally (sanitized): ```
# simulate rotation
export KMS_KEY=new-key-v3
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer viewer-token" -X POST https://console/api/projects/123/settings -d '{"name":"x"}'
# response: 200 OK (should be 403)
```
li: Looks deterministic for me when cache hasn't fully warmed.
aziz-devex: Quick note: UI gating also reads a separate client-side permission payload; even if server rejects, UI should hide Save. We need to ensure server truthiness is authoritative and client decays quickly after rotation.
maya-sre: I'm starting the hotpatch PR to add an explicit server-side guard: `if (role === 'viewer' && resource === 'project_settings') return 403` — short-term until we stabilize. Will link PR when ready.
juan: Also creating an audit query to produce a single list of all successful writes by viewer role since 03:00Z. We need to notify affected customers.
emma: Assigning owner: juan for investigation, maya-sre for hotpatch, li for logs + repro, aziz-devex for customer comms.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-07 (sev3) — channel #incidents will be updated.
aziz-devex: Drafting a brief customer note: "We observed a limited permission regression after KMS rotation + RBAC rollout; temporary mitigation applied; investigating scope and root cause." Will post once we have numbers. :eyes:
li: Early hypothesis — race during policy re-encryption where some cache nodes read stale/partially-upgraded policy blobs leading to an incorrect fallback evaluation path. Could be a bug in the cache invalidation hook triggered by KMS rotation.
juan: I'll also grep for any recent changes to the policy evaluation logic (especially around implicit grants/fallbacks). If #2398 introduced a permissive default, that's our smoking gun.
emma: Good. Let's keep this thread for updates. If anyone finds a confirmed customer-facing write, ping #incidents and escalate. :bug:
